skill.name: consent-registry
skill.description: Records subscriber consent facts, lawful basis, opt-in proof, and suppression events in a durable consent registry for email programs.
skill.summary: Maintain a durable email consent and suppression registry.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, relative documentation links, and homepage metadata. One real medium-risk issue remains: an optional live Resend connector command can mutate external suppression state. The skill also handles persistent subscriber consent records, so privacy minimization and retention controls are required.

remediation.issue: Optional live Resend sync can mutate external ESP state.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before --live, pass subscriber identifiers as separate arguments, and keep dry-run as the default.

remediation.issue: Consent records can contain subscriber identifiers and proof.
remediation.suggestion: Store minimized or hashed identifiers, record only required proof, and document retention rules for memory/consent/.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples and links trigger noisy static findings.
remediation.suggestion: Label prompt examples as non-shell text and separate operational connector commands from reference prose.

content.value_statement: Email teams need durable proof of consent and opt-out history. This skill records lawful basis, source, proof, and suppression events for each subscriber.
actual_capabilities: Create or update one consent record per subscriber under memory/consent/.
Record opt-in timestamps, lawful basis, acquisition source, and double opt-in proof.
Append unsubscribe, hard bounce, complaint, and re-subscribe events with dates and sources.
Reconcile pending consent candidates from list imports.
Route send approval and suppression segment decisions to downstream skills.
Promote missing basis and suppression pointers to hot cache or open loops.
limitations: Does not decide whether a campaign is safe or legal to send.
Does not build or apply suppression segments.
Requires user-provided exports or pasted source records.
Can store personal data, so projects need consent and retention controls.

use_cases.title: Log Opt-In Proof
use_cases.description: Record a subscriber opt-in with date, source, lawful basis, and double opt-in proof.

use_cases.title: Update Suppression History
use_cases.description: Append unsubscribe, bounce, complaint, or re-subscribe events from an ESP export.

use_cases.title: Reconcile Imported Candidates
use_cases.description: Review pending consent candidates and resolve missing basis or identity conflicts.

prompt_templates.title: Record One Opt-In
prompt_templates.prompt: Record opt-in for this subscriber. Use this signup date, source, lawful basis, and double opt-in proof.

prompt_templates.title: Log Opt-Out Events
prompt_templates.prompt: Log these unsubscribe, hard bounce, and complaint events from our ESP export. Keep each event dated and sourced.

prompt_templates.title: Answer Consent Status
prompt_templates.scenario: Compliance lookup before routing to an auditor
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether this subscriber has a consent record. Report status, basis, opt-in date, proof, and suppression history only.

prompt_templates.title: Reconcile Import Candidates
prompt_templates.prompt: Reconcile the pending consent candidates from our import. Mark missing basis, identity conflicts, and processed records clearly.

output_examples.input: Record opt-in for a new form signup with double opt-in proof.
output_examples.output: Created one consent record. The subscriber is subscribed, basis is consent, and proof is attached from the form signup.

output_examples.input: Log an unsubscribe and a spam complaint from the latest ESP export.
output_examples.output: Updated two records. One subscriber is unsubscribed, one is suppressed, and both events include dates and export sources.

output_examples.input: Check whether this imported contact has a lawful basis on file.
output_examples.output: No lawful basis is on file. The record needs input before any send approval or suppression workflow continues.

best_practices: Ask before the first project write and keep consent records minimized.
Store dates, sources, and proof for every consent or suppression fact.
Route send approval and suppression segment work to the named downstream skills.
anti_patterns: Do not infer consent from a purchased list or imported claim.
Do not overwrite opt-out history with a single clean or risky label.
Do not use this skill to approve sends or build suppression segments.

faq.question: What does this skill store?
faq.answer: It stores subscriber consent status, lawful basis, opt-in proof, source, and suppression event history.

faq.question: Can it approve an email send?
faq.answer: No. It records facts only and routes send approval to the email quality auditor.

faq.question: Can it build a suppression segment?
faq.answer: No. It records suppression facts and routes segment application to list segment builder.

faq.question: Does it require an ESP API?
faq.answer: No. It can work from pasted records or manual exports.

faq.question: How does it handle missing consent?
faq.answer: It records no basis on file and asks for input. It does not treat missing records as opt-in.

faq.question: Is personal data involved?
faq.answer: Yes. Use minimized identifiers, clear sources, and project retention controls.
